key_insight: Delafossite and ordered rock-salt ABO2 oxides can compete with infinite-layer nickelates in stability, with delafossites especially competitive for Ni/Pd/Pt systems and a strong reversal in cation/electronic character.
engineering_relevance: The results help narrow synthesis targets and substrate/doping choices for stabilizing bulk or film infinite-layer oxides relevant to next-generation correlated-electron and superconducting devices.
method: High-throughput first-principles calculations across the AB O2 oxide landscape
Phase-stability comparison among infinite-layer, delafossite, and ordered rock-salt (111) variants
Electronic-structure analysis of Fermi-surface and orbital character under different cation/doping choices
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a computed phase diagram and comparative electronic-structure results showing delafossite stability rivaling infinite-layer phases, with La–Ni emerging as the thermodynamic optimum and Ca/Sr/Ba hole doping further stabilizing the infinite-layer motif.
watch_item: These are computational stability trends, so experimental realizability may still depend strongly on epitaxial strain, growth conditions, and kinetic barriers not fully captured by thermodynamics alone.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
